analysis:
Integration pass over the progress-display rewrite. Changed files: ModelDownloadProgress.swift (ProgressRenderer and ManifestDownloadProgress), ModelDownloader+Download.swift, the new ModelDownloadProgressTests.swift, a changelog and a docs paragraph. I replayed the ModelDownloader+Download.swift patch (head hunks around lines 126-166) and the changelog and docs text directly. I did not see the ModelDownloadProgress.swift body or the test file, so I relied on the earlier analyses for those.

In ModelDownloader+Download.swift the per-file closure is factored into a shared `transfer` closure. It calls progress.start(label:), then downloadManifestFileWithResume, then progress.complete, in the original order. The only behavioral additions are `await renderTask.value` after `renderTask.cancel()` on both the success and catch paths, and the start() hook. Verification and publish logic is untouched: validateArtifactManifest, per-file hash and size checks, the aggregate hash check in finalizeStagedManifest, staging cleanup on failure, and resume via .part. So the weight-integrity threats (A-004, T-012, T-027) are unaffected.

No change touches the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), attestation or App Attest (TB-009, TB-011), keys, the prefix cache (T-041), inference, or billing. I found no new network, filesystem, authorization or crypto surface.

Residual unverified items, none established as findings:
1. Manifest-path labels are printed raw to the terminal. The base did the same, so any escape-sequence injection is pre-existing, and manifest path sanitization is outside the supplied evidence.
2. Awaiting renderTask.value assumes the render loop honors cancellation. The earlier analysis says it checks Task.isCancelled, but I did not see that loop body. The impact would be at most a local CLI hang.
3. Eight source units were omitted from replay, so I could not directly re-verify the renderer implementation.

No security regression is identified.
